data.body: Phase 1 RCA confirmed. Dynamic experiment: for each executing nested launcher, the parent process was given its own --basetemp while PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT pointed at an isolated shared root containing pytest-0..pytest-3 and a byte sentinel in pytest-0. Both outer tests returned rc=0, yet the sentinel was deleted: tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py::test_engine_submodules_resolve_when_the_tests_unit_shadow_is_active and tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py::test_repro_module_passes_standalone. This observes the exact mechanism: each outer test launches a second pytest without --basetemp; repository autouse tmp_path fixtures force that child to allocate a user-numbered root, register cleanup_numbered_dir, and delete the unrelated cleanup-eligible pytest-0 at session finish. The pinned implementation basis is uv.lock:2403-2404 (pytest 9.1.1) and upstream _pytest/tmpdir.py getbasetemp / pytest_sessionfinish. Rival explanations were rejected because the outer session had an explicit basetemp, both target tests themselves stayed green, and only the unowned inner child could reach PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT. Defect legitimacy: defect; the existing isolation invariant is encoded by tests/unit/test_test_suite_store_isolation.py::test_nested_pytest_does_not_clean_shared_numbered_temp_root and the parent-owned precedents at tests/_store_isolation.py:32-48 and tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py:62-78. Caller-dependency sweep: these are leaf pytest tests; no caller relies on deleting unrelated temp trees. The three collect-only launchers are not siblings at runtime because TempPathFactory._basetemp remains None, and pytester-managed launches already inject basetemp. Phase 2 is unlocked.
